basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 12.' and it opens 'VERS. 12.-- Recordatus autem Dominus Noe, adduxit spiritum super terram, et imminutae'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 12.-- Recordatus autem Dominus Noe, adduxit spiritum super terram, et imminutae sunt aquae. De illo spiritu intelligi potest de quo dictum est: Spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas. Tunc enim ferebatur ut, congregatis aquis, in suum [ Z., in unum] locum terra apparuisset. Nunc autem adductus dicitur, ut ablatis de medio aquis diluvii faciem terrae revelaret. Potest et spiritus nomine ventus intelligi, juxta illud Psalmistae: Et stetit spiritus procellae (Psal. CVI, 25), cujus flatibus crebris aqua cogeretur recedere.
